author: Inside Edition
description: A mystery for more than 40 years finally has an answer, uncovered in part by students on a college campus. The Ramapo College Investigative Genetic Genealogy Center worked with the New Jersey State police to identify remains found in a shallow grave in Salem County back in 1979. In this case, they were able to give this John Doe a name: Robert Dean Irelan. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: NJ College Helps Police Identify Human Remains Found In 1979

author: Inside Edition
description: Being absolutely adorable is a tough job, but this baby is up for the challenge. An adorable pudu fawn has arrived at the San Diego Zoo Safari Park. Native to South America, pudus are one of the tiniest deer species in the world. They typically grow to be 13 to 17 inches tall and will weigh between 10 and 25 lbs, depending on the species. Which is the size of a house cat or small breed dog. Inside Edition Digital has more.
title: One Of The Smallest Deer Species Born At San Diego Park

author: Inside Edition
description: Dozens of people were laid to rest in Iowa over the weekend. None of the deceased had family to see them off; all of these remains were unclaimed. A non-profit organization called Final Salute stepped in to help. The group enlists caring strangers to serve as friends and family, to give those who have passed a dignified farewell. One mourner remarked at the graveside, "This is our moment to acknowledge them, to ensure they are seen, heard, and remembered."
title: Dozens Of Unclaimed Remains Laid To Rest By Caring Strangers

author: Inside Edition
description: The eldest son of famed director Rob Reiner and wife Michelle is breaking his silence four months after their murders, allegedly at the hands of their son Nick. Nick Reiner has pled not guilty to the charges.
title: Jake Reiner Says Parents' Deaths Are 'Too Devastating To Comprehend'

author: Inside Edition
description: Law enforcement is working to piece together the motives and actions of Cole Allen, the suspect in this weekend's shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, DC. President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump, as well as several cabinet officials and a host of journalists, were gathered at the Saturday evening event when shots rang out. A suspect bearing firearms had breached security on a different floor of the Washington Hilton.
title: White House Correspondents' Dinner Shooting Suspect Due In Court

author: Inside Edition
description: Inside Edition's Sal Bono digs into the tragic story of city councilman James E. Davis, an outspoken voice against gun violence.
title: The Political Assassination That Shocked NYC #shorts
